title: Interpretable Orthogonal Latent Diffusion with Scale-Selective Uncertainty for Medical Image Super-Resolution
abstract: arXiv:2611.32135v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Diffusion models are increasingly used for medical image reconstruction and super-resolution, but their samples may contain plausible fine-scale hallucinations that are difficult to identify from the reconstructed image alone. We propose Med-PODiff, a patch-wise proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) diffusion framework for brain MRI super-resolution that performs generative reconstruction in compact and interpretable local coefficient spaces. Unlike pixel-space or learned-latent diffusion models, Med-PODiff uses the POD structure to separate low-rank anatomical variation from fine-detail residual variation, enabling predictive uncertainty to be decomposed into total, coarse, and fine components. Building on this decomposition, we define a pixel-wise hallucination-risk score, $H_p$, that emphasizes regions where fine-detail uncertainty dominates coarse structural uncertainty. On brain MRI, Med-PODiff outperforms representative diffusion

tldr: 提出Med-PODiff分块POD扩散框架，将预测不确定性分解为粗细两个尺度并定义逐像素幻觉风险评分，用于脑部MRI超分辨率中的细尺度幻觉识别。
en_tdlr: Med-PODiff, a patch-wise POD diffusion framework that decomposes predictive uncertainty into coarse and fine scales and defines a pixel-wise hallucination-risk score to identify fine-scale hallucinations in brain MRI super-resolution.
